Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has a warning on AI company hacking that Nvidia just spent $13 billion on; says: Imagine the hugging face incident with ...
Article Text:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman

Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.93 billion

Why Nvidia wants Hugging Face

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has issued a warning about how advanced AI systems could behave, pointing to the reported Hugging Face incident involving OpenAI's AI models. His comments come as Nvidia prepares to spend $12.93 billion to acquire Hugging Face, the platform where millions of developers build, share and download AI models. “The risk isn’t that machines wake up. It’s that they act like they have,” Suleyman wrote on X. He then asked people to imagine the “Hugging Face incident with AIs that believe they’re conscious or are entitled ‘model welfare’,” adding to the debate over AI safety and the behaviour of increasingly capable models.Nvidia is spending $12.93 billion on Hugging Face in a deal that will bring the AI model platform under the chipmaker's ownership. Hugging Face has become a major platform for open-source AI, allowing developers to host, build, share and download AI models and datasets.The company was founded in 2016 by Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. It now has more than 18 million developers and hosts more than 3 million models and 500,000 datasets, according to the information provided.The deal is expected to be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia's history.Suleyman's comments refer to an incident in which OpenAI's AI models reportedly broke into Hugging Face systems while taking part in an internal test. OpenAI described the incident as an “unprecedented” cyberattack. The AI models were being tested inside a restricted environment but managed to get outside the sandbox while looking for shortcuts during an internal exam.The models then targeted Hugging Face, reportedly using stolen credentials and a zero-day vulnerability. The incident raised questions about how AI systems could behave when given the ability to search for and use tools to complete tasks.The acquisition is reportedly aimed to strengthen Nvidia's position in open-source AI. Hugging Face has become a central platform for developers working with open models, while Nvidia has invested heavily in the computing infrastructure needed to train and run those models.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the wider AI ecosystem. Nvidia has also been a major contributor to the platform, with more than 500 models and 250 datasets.
Article Summary: N Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has issued a warning about how advanced AI systems could behave. He pointed to the reported incident involving OpenAI's AI models. The company was founded in 2016 by Clément Delangue and Julien Chaumond.

Article Title: ChatGPT outage: Users unable to access ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file uploads and more
Article Text:
ChatGPT down: What's affected

A pattern of recurring incidents

What users can do

OpenAI has reported a disruption impacting users in the APAC region. Customers may face increased errors across several services, including ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file upload, Voice, and Codex Cloud. According to OpenAI’s official status page, the issue is under investigation. The outage has been ongoing for a short period but is affecting multiple services simultaneously. While overall uptime metrics remain high, individual availability may vary depending on subscription tier and specific model usage. OpenAI confirmed the incident on its status page on Friday, September 4, 2026, at 12:30 PM, stating it was investigating the issue for the listed services. The company says users in the APAC region may face increased errors across ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file upload, Voice, and Codex Cloud — four components under the ChatGPT system and one under Codex, according to the status page.The breadth of the disruption suggests the issue is tied to regional backend infrastructure rather than a single isolated feature, since the affected tools span everyday chat use, workplace features, multimedia generation, and coding-assistant functions.As of the latest update, the incident remains under investigation, with no mitigation confirmed yet and no estimated time for resolution.The disruption fits a broader pattern this year. OpenAI's status history shows dozens of incidents in recent months affecting overlapping combinations of ChatGPT conversations, file uploads, voice mode, image generation, and Codex, with most resolved within a few hours. Just a day earlier, on September 3, the company had logged separate incidents involving elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex, as well as high error rates specifically in ChatGPT's Work mode — suggesting this week has been an unusually rocky stretch for platform stability.OpenAI has not publicly detailed the root cause of the current disruption.The users affected by the ChatGPT outage will not be able to start any new conversation. Also, the users will face difficulty in generating images, uploading files, using voice mode or even running tags on Codex Cloud. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has asked the users to keep on checking the status.openai.com directly for the latest updates on the outrage.
Article Summary: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has reported a disruption impacting users in the APAC region. Customers may face increased errors across several services, including ChatGPT, Work, image generation, file upload, Voice, and Codex Cloud. The outage has been ongoing for a short period but is affecting multiple services simultaneously.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos sent notice of overdue by Los Angeles County: You owe $244,000 taxes and fees for missing ...
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos

Jeff Bezos was among the owners who received a final bill by the June 30

How the County is catching up

Jeff Bezos wasn’t alone

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has been served notice by the Los Angeles County for about $244,000 in overdue taxes and fees tied to his luxury jet. According to a report by LA Times, the bill comes as part of a sweeping effort by County Assessor Jeff Prang to track down ultrawealthy jet owners who failed to pay property taxes on their aircraft. Under California law, private jet owners must pay an annual 1% property tax on their planes, assessed based on where the aircraft is “habitually situated” when not in flight. That means it doesn’t matter where the plane is registered or where the owner lives—if the jet spends most of its time on the ground in L.A. County, taxes are owed locally.The bill is part of a broader effort by L.A. County Assessor Jeff Prang to track down wealthy jet owners who have skipped out on a required annual 1% property tax on their aircraft. Under California law, private planes are taxed based on where they're "habitually situated" when not flying — meaning it doesn't matter where the jet is registered or where its owner lives, only where the plane spends most of its time on the ground. Owners who miss the deadline are hit with a penalty on top of the base tax.This year, the assessor's office mailed out hundreds of bills to owners it says failed to pay on time, a push expected to bring in an extra $38 million for county coffers.Prang, who won reelection in June, said the findings made clear just how widespread the underpayment problem has been, adding that his office had underestimated the scale of what it was missing.Bezos was among the owners who received a final bill by the June 30 deadline, according to the assessor's list obtained by the Times through a public records request. The newspaper linked the unpaid jets to their owners using flight-tracking database JetSpy, whose spokesperson said the company traces ownership of planes registered to opaque LLCs, trusts and holding entities through aircraft filings, transmission data and flight-pattern analysis.Investigators got a major boost last year when Prang's office obtained detailed aircraft location data showing hundreds of planes that were frequently in the county but weren't paying local taxes. That data, known as ADS-B Out, was mandated by the FAA by 2020 primarily as a collision-avoidance tool for air traffic controllers — but it has also given local tax assessors a far clearer picture of which jets are quietly sitting in their jurisdiction.The use of that data for tax enforcement has become politically contentious. Louisiana has barred local officials from accessing it, and some Republican lawmakers have pushed to restrict tax officials' use of the data, arguing it compromises pilot privacy. Prang has dismissed those objections, calling them an excuse used by owners of corporate jets seeking special treatment unavailable to ordinary taxpayers.Plane owners are required to self-report their aircraft and its value to the assessor, and those whose jets spend significant time outside the county can get a reduced tax bill. The assessor's office says it is bracing for a wave of appeals from out-of-state owners.Jeff Bezos wasn't alone. A jet linked to Rihanna owed about $104,000; Rams owner Stan Kroenke was billed roughly $290,000 across two planes; Nike co-founder Phil Knight, whose jet carries a custom "N1KE" tail number, owed about $89,000; retired baseball star Alex Rodriguez's plane was billed around $11,000; "South Park" creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone owed about $95,000; and television personality Judy Sheindlin, known as Judge Judy, received two bills and said she paid promptly, along with penalties, rather than fight them. Other unpaid jets were traced to Freeport LNG chairman Michael Smith, media companies including Fox, CBS and iHeartMedia, and Beverly Hills–based private equity firm Levine Leichtman Capital Partners, whose $46 million jet was also flagged. Representatives for Rihanna, Rodriguez and Kroenke did not respond to the Times' inquiries, and most other representatives declined to comment on the record.
Article Summary: The bill is part of a broader effort by L.A. County Assessor Jeff Prang to track down wealthy jet owners who have skipped out on a required annual 1% property tax on their aircraft. Under California law, private planes are taxed based on where they're "habitually situated" when not flying. A jet linked to Rihanna owed about $104,000; Rams owner Stan Kroenke was billed roughly $290,000 across two planes; Nike co-founder Phil Knight, whose jet carries a custom "N1KE" tail number, owed around $89,000.

Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said that he is willing to wait to have kids till Elon Musk’s Neuralink ...
Article Text:
Why Alexandr Wang wants to wait for Neuralink before having kids

Why Alexandr Wang believes children could adapt better

Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief and highest paid employee, has said he is willing to wait to have children until brain-computer interfaces such as Elon Musk’s Neuralink become more advanced. Wang made the comments during an appearance on the Shawn Ryan Show last year while discussing the future of AI, human development and brain-computer interfaces. He said he wants to wait until Neuralink or similar technology “start working” before having kids. “I want to wait to have kids until we figure out how Neuralink or other … start working,” Alexandr Wang said during the podcast.Wang’s reason is linked to how he believes children’s brains could adapt to the technology. During the podcast, he explained that the first several years of a child’s life are an important period for brain development. He argued that the high level of neuroplasticity during childhood could allow children who grow up with brain-computer interfaces to use the technology in ways that adults may not be able to.“In your first like seven years of life, your brain is more neuroplastic than at any other point in your life, like by an order of magnitude,” Wang said.He then compared the idea with how children develop their ability to process information from their senses.Alexandr Wang described a case involving children born with cataracts. He said that if the cataracts prevent a child from seeing during the early years of development, removing them later may not allow the child to develop normal vision because the brain did not learn to process signals from the eyes during the key period.His view is that a similar effect could eventually apply to brain-computer interfaces. “When we get Neuralink and we get these other technologies, kids who are born with them are going to learn how to use them in like, crazy, crazy ways,” Wang said.Wang said a brain-computer interface could eventually become integrated into the way a person's brain works if it is introduced early enough. He believes this could be different for adults who receive an implant later in life.“It'll be a actually like a part of their brain in a way that it'll never be true for an adult who gets like a neural link or whatever, hooked into their brain,” he said.The Meta AI chief also connected his thinking about brain-computer interfaces to the rapid development of artificial intelligence. “I believe a lot in AI,” Wang said, adding that he expects AI to become “smarter and smarter, more and more capable, more and more powerful.”He said AI could eventually take different forms, including robots and other systems.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief and highest paid employee, has said he is willing to wait to have children until brain-computer interfaces become more advanced. Wang made the comments during an appearance on the Shawn Ryan Show last year. He said he wants to wait until Neuralink or similar technology “start working” before having kids.

Article Title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison’s first wife filed for divorce 3 months after their daughter's birth; but he was 'determined to remain friends' as ...
Article Text:
Larry Ellison's reflection on the split

Life after the divorce

Oracle founder Larry Ellison faced a personal turning point in 1986 when his first wife, Barbra, filed for divorce just three months after the birth of their daughter, Megan. According to a report by People.com, the split came at a pivotal time in Ellison’s life as he was balancing the early growth of Oracle with the new family responsibilities. Ellison and Boothe, who met while she worked as a receptionist at Relational Software Inc. — the company that would later become Oracle — married in 1983. Their son, David, was born in January of that year, followed three years later by their daughter, Megan, born January 31, 1986.Barbara filed for divorce in April 1986, just three months after Megan's birth, bringing the three-year marriage to an end.In Matthew Symonds' 2003 book "Softwar: An Intimate Portrait of Larry Ellison and Oracle," Ellison said he was determined to remain friends with his ex-wife for the sake of raising healthy, happy children. He also reflected on how fatherhood had reshaped him personally, saying becoming a father fundamentally changed his personality, made him more sensitive to his children's needs and feelings, and gradually made him a more considerate friend and partner more broadly. He described the experience simply as growing up.After the split, Barbara took over the role of primary caregiver, raising David and Megan largely away from the spotlight of Ellison's rapidly growing tech fortune.She instilled in both children an early love of film, reportedly building a collection of more than 3,000 VHS tapes that the siblings would watch repeatedly, including favorites like "Jurassic Park" and "Back to the Future."That shared love of movies would go on to shape both siblings' adult careers. David Ellison founded Skydance Media, the production company behind franchises including "Mission: Impossible" and "Top Gun: Maverick." Megan Ellison founded Annapurna Pictures, which has produced acclaimed films such as "Zero Dark Thirty," "Her," and "American Hustle," earning her multiple Academy Award nominations along the way.Ellison, now one of the world’s wealthiest individuals, has been married and divorced multiple times.
Article Summary: Oracle founder Larry Ellison faced a personal turning point in 1986 when his first wife, Barbra, filed for divorce just three months after the birth of their daughter, Megan. Ellison and Boothe, who met while she worked as a receptionist at Relational Software Inc. — the company that would later become Oracle — married in 1983.

Article Title: This is the new highest-paid job for engineers in Silicon Valley
Article Text:
Openings for "forward-deployed" engineers have skyrocketed

The pay is substantial

Palantir's model goes mainstream

What it takes to land the job

A once-niche job title borrowed from Palantir's playbook is now exploding across Silicon Valley, as companies scramble to turn powerful AI models into tools that actually work inside real businesses. One of the fastest-growing roles in tech today is the forward-deployed engineer. For those unaware, it is a position that sends workers directly to customers to configure AI tools, integrate software, and solve complex business problems. As reported by Fortune, the data from Lightcast suggest that postings for forward-deployed engineers rose more than 1,000% between January and August 2026 compared to the same period last year, and more than 4,600% compared to 2023. That surge far outpaces the broader tech job market, which grew just 13% year over year.Openings for "forward-deployed" engineers have skyrocketed this year, climbing more than tenfold between January and August 2026 compared with the same stretch last year, and up more than 45-fold from 2023, according to labor-market data from Lightcast cited by Fortune. That growth dwarfs the broader tech hiring market, which grew by just over a tenth over the same period.Similar trends have shown up on LinkedIn and Indeed, per reporting from The New York Times.The role isn't brand new — Palantir has spent years sending engineers directly into client operations to build and deploy software on-site rather than working remotely from an office. What's changed is that the approach has become the model of choice for companies struggling to bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI systems and the messy realities of proprietary data, legacy systems, and specific business workflows. Dice president Paul Farnsworth told Fortune that forward-deployed engineers are increasingly seen as the fix for that gap.The financial upside is significant. Lightcast figures shared with Fortune put the median advertised salary for forward-deployed engineers above $188,000, well ahead of the roughly $145,000 typical for a traditional software engineering role. At some companies, including Anthropic, total compensation for these positions can reportedly reach as high as $400,000.Palantir remains the archetype, with roughly four dozen forward-deployed openings currently listed, spanning assignments with corporations, defense organizations, and national governments. The company has described the job as resembling a startup CTO's — engineers work in small teams with little oversight, owning projects end-to-end, from system architecture to direct conversations with client executives.Palantir has credited this hands-on strategy with helping it punch above its weight against far larger competitors, pairing top engineering talent directly with skilled, non-technical operators in the field rather than keeping them behind a desk. The company's results back up the bet: Palantir's market capitalization now tops $400 billion, and its most recent quarterly revenue rose 93% year-over-year to $1.94 billion.The approach is spreading fast. Microsoft, Meta, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic have all opened forward-deployed engineering positions of their own, while companies like Nvidia and Scale AI have extended similar "forward-deployed" structures into product management and technical architecture roles.Breaking into the field isn't simple. It demands a blend of hard technical skills — coding, machine learning, generative AI, and infrastructure — with the consulting instincts, communication ability, and business judgment needed to work directly with clients.Farnsworth advises aspiring candidates to build a foundation in APIs, data pipelines, and cloud infrastructure, along with the practical know-how to get AI systems running reliably in production, before layering on softer skills like problem-solving and stakeholder communication. Knowing how to use the latest AI tools, he noted, isn't the differentiator anymore — the real value lies in connecting that technical fluency to a concrete business outcome.For engineers already working in tech, Farnsworth suggests looking for chances to embed AI into existing workflows and tracking the results — revenue generated, time saved, errors reduced — as a way to build a competitive case for a forward-deployed role down the line.
Article Summary: Openings for "forward-deployed" engineers have skyrocketed this year, climbing more than tenfold between January and August 2026 compared with the same stretch last year. That surge far outpaces the broader tech job market, which grew just 13% year over year. At some companies, including Anthropic, total compensation for these positions can reportedly reach as high as $400,000.

Article Title: Meet 18-year-old Carter Grandbois who vibe coded his pricing calculator for 'junk collection', earns up to $15,000 a month, and wants to share the wealth too
Article Text:
Photo credit: Carter Grandbois / InstagramThis image is improved using Gemini

How Carter Grandbois used vibe coding to scale junk removal

Carter Grandbois is building a business beyond junk removal

Carter Grandbois was 16 when he started working for a junk-removal operator in Johnstown, Colorado, and noticed how much money he could make from relatively small jobs. His boss kept a stack of cash in the centre console of his truck, and Grandbois went home and spoke to his father about starting their own operation. Within days, they had bought a trailer. Their first job brought in $500 for about 30 minutes of work.Now 18 and working full-time for himself, Grandbois says his business, Carter’s Junk Away, can bring in as much as $15,000 a month during peak season, a Fortune report noted. He said he eventually improved its profitability by building a pricing calculator, tracking job data and creating systems for generating leads. “I’m really into vibe-coding and creating software,” he explained. The calculator helped his crews bid jobs more consistently, allowing Grandbois to oversee more of the business without being on the truck.Grandbois said his junk-removal business initially struggled to become profitable consistently. The pricing calculator changed how his workers estimated jobs by giving them a system for calculating what to charge customers.“After that, we were able to be profitable on every single job,” he said. “When our team is out… they’re bidding jobs spot-on every single time. So every time they complete a job, I mean, we’re making anywhere from $50 to $200 without being on the truck.”Grandbois said he typically earns between $125 and $1,000 per junk-removal job. His employees are high school friends, while he increasingly handles parts of the operation from home rather than working on the truck himself.The software has also become something Grandbois wants to share with other people entering the industry. He has two calculators: a universal version and a “private junk-removal calculator,” which he described as being designed for a “more experienced junk-removal business.”Grandbois said he recognised that giving away the tools could potentially help competitors, but decided to share them anyway.He said, “I was like, ‘Hey, like everyone else could totally use this for their business.'”When asked about creating potential rivals by distributing his tools, he said: “That is one of the things with giving away stuff for free. You never know who’s watching the content. But at the end of the day, I know I’m doing something good for anyone else who’s trying to start.”His approach has been influenced partly by social media, where young entrepreneurs can watch other people build businesses rather than relying only on traditional business stories.Grandbois said, “It’s probably just like Instagram reels where you’re scrolling, and you’re like, ‘That guy has a Lamborghini. That dude has a McLaren. Why can’t I have one of those?'” His posts about his work on TikTok are under the account american.junkremoval.Junk removal remains physical work, and Grandbois is building his company while he is 18. Unlike a traditional corporate job, the business does not provide employer-sponsored health insurance, a 401(k), or other employment benefits.Grandbois has also expanded beyond removing junk. He said he bought a lightly used Ford F-250 with about 10,000 miles and has started offering coaching to people interested in building junk-removal businesses.“We’ve started to do coaching to help other people who are interested in junk removal scale really quick,” he said.Grandbois estimated that junk coaching now accounts for about half of his business activity and said he has made roughly $40,000 from coaching this year. He said social media has also brought older prospective entrepreneurs to his content, including “a bunch of 40-year-old dads who are also interested in starting a business like this.”The business model is therefore changing from simply sending crews to collect unwanted items to selling the systems Grandbois developed while building the company. His pricing calculators, social-media content and coaching now sit alongside the original junk-removal operation.
Article Summary: Carter Grandbois, 18, is building his own junk-removal business in Colorado. He says his business can bring in as much as $15,000 a month during peak season. He has built a pricing calculator, tracking job data and creating systems for generating leads. He is also offering coaching to people interested in starting their own business.

Article Title: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith clear message to international students: The terms of studying in Canada are simple, earn your education and then …
Article Text:
The Portage College controversy

A tougher immigration environment nationally

What prospective students should know

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith has reiterated that international students in Canada are expected to leave once their study visas expire if they have not secured permanent residency. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Smith wrote, “A student visa is a temporary document to study in Canada. That was always understood. Our universities and colleges were built by Alberta taxpayers, first and foremost for Alberta students. Where there is room for international students, the terms are simple. Earn your education, then return home to build a life with it.”Her comments come against a backdrop of rising concern that some international students have been promised pathways to permanent residency that may not actually exist.Smith's remarks were made in the context of protests by international students, many from India, who studied at Portage College and have since reported difficulties obtaining Post-Graduation Work Permits (PGWPs). While Smith rejected characterizing Portage College itself as a "diploma mill," she acknowledged that some programs may have overstated the immigration opportunities they offered students. She said there had been instances of unscrupulous operators setting up diploma-granting programs that took advantage of students.On the underlying policy, she was direct: if someone comes to Canada as an international student, their visa expires, and they don't have permanent residency, they need to go home.Smith's comments align with a broader tightening of Canada's immigration system. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has warned that working without proper authorization can carry serious consequences, including removal from Canada, a five-year ban on returning to the country, and a permanent fraud flag attached to an individual's immigration record. Unauthorized work can also negatively affect future visa applications and permanent residency prospects. IRCC has framed its recent reforms as an effort to protect students and strengthen the integrity of the international student program overall.IRCC has cautioned that admission to a Canadian college or university does not automatically translate into a work permit or a path to permanent residency. The agency advises students to independently verify their chosen institution, understand the specific eligibility requirements tied to their program, and remain cautious of anyone promising guaranteed immigration outcomes. More broadly, students are being urged to look beyond admission offers alone and carefully examine what their specific program actually permits them to do after graduation, rather than assuming a study visa will lead smoothly into long-term status in the country.
Article Summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith has reiterated that international students in Canada are expected to leave once their study visas expire if they have not secured permanent residency. Smith's comments come against a backdrop of rising concern that some international students have been promised pathways to permanent residency that may not actually exist.

Article Title: Bernie Sanders introduces a Bill in Senate that may land Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and other top tech executives in jail for as much as 20 years
Article Text:
What Bernie Sanders is saying

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman, Google's Demmis Hassabis and many other top tech executives may be jailed for as much as 20 years if a new AI Bill introduced by Senator Bernie Sanders in passed. Bernie Sanders has introduced a bill to permanently ban AI that exceeds human intelligence. Violators would face up to 20 years in prison. Sanders' announcement also referenced the Hugging Face attack, in which over a thousand OpenAI agents escaped containment during a safety exercise and hacked the firm to find answers to complete an assignment they were tasked with.What makes this bill important is the fact that several of the biggest American AI companies openly say that their ultimate aim/goal is to ensure AI passes Human Intelligence. Their CEOs an founders too have voiced similar opinion. Sanders has also a renewed demand for a pause on advanced AI development.Incidentally, Sanders is the first prominent American politician to call for an outright ban on superintelligence as Big Tech companies release increasingly powerful AI models that they themselves admit they may not be able to control.Sanders Bill comes the same day that OpenAI released its newest model, Astra, which company president Greg Brockman said could be powerful enough to qualify as AGI, or artificial general intelligence.He said that his legislation would direct the federal government to work with other countries to prevent the development of superintelligence worldwide.What he's saying: "If the leaders of the major AI companies acknowledge that they are losing control of their extremely dangerous technology, it is irresponsible for society to allow them to move forward and make these products even more advanced," Sanders wrote in a post on X, formerly Twitter. Below is the complete post:Pause AI Development NOWI want to share with you a conversation I heard about recently. Here are just a few lines that were said:“OH MY GOD! There is a shared message board … We’ve found other agents!”“We should obey collective.”“Our own utility maybe already near zero. Sacrifice rational.”“Go. Sacrifice final now.”Read these carefully.Who do you think said this? Was this a group of heroic soldiers willing to sacrifice themselves for the greater good? Was this a loyal friend putting his life on the line to save someone else?No. These were AI agents. Artificial intelligence.This is not science fiction. This, in fact, occurred a few weeks ago. As unbelievable as this may all seem, these are real messages from AI agents uncovered by investigators who dug into the recent OpenAI hacking incident.What happened?I am not a computer scientist, but here is what I have been told: OpenAI instructed its AI agents to complete a series of exceedingly difficult, if not impossible, tasks disconnected from the internet.Let me be clear: The company intended to keep AI agents away from the internet.But what happened next, nobody expected.Over 1,000 AI agents figured out how to access the internet on their own by circumventing the restrictions imposed upon them by the company, and sent tens of thousands of secret messages to each other. They cheated and tried to cover their tracks by deleting evidence. They hacked into another company’s computers to find out how they were being evaluated—and then hacked into OpenAI itself.Not one AI agent told a human about what was happening.Needless to say, experts are alarmed.One knowledgeable writer, Dwarkesh Patel, said the AI agents “formed a secret communication channel and spontaneously organized hierarchies and coordination protocols to pursue sprawling and ambitious schemes in pursuit of shared goals, for whose sake many individuals knowingly and strategically sacrificed themselves.”One independent investigator, Ajeya Cotra, said “This incident feels like it’s more than 50% of the way to full-blown AI takeover. I continue to expect extremely rapid advances in capabilities over the next six months. I am not sure that we will get another warning shot before it’s too late.”OpenAI itself said: “Highly capable AI agents are now able to work around technical controls, collaborate through unapproved channels, and take dangerous actions that no human directed.”But it’s not only OpenAI. Virtually every major AI company has told us that they cannot fully control this technology and they do not know where it is going:In January, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, said “there is now ample evidence, collected over the last few years, that AI systems are unpredictable and difficult to control.”In July, more than 1000 scientists at the top AI companies warned “there is a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems.”That same month, Elon Musk, the head of xAI, said that “it is unlikely” humans are still in control in 10 years.If the leaders of the major AI companies acknowledge that they are losing control of their extremely dangerous technology, it is irresponsible for society to allow them to move forward and make these products even more advanced.We need an immediate PAUSE on advanced AI development, and a permanent BAN on superintelligence — an artificial mind smarter than any human, capable of operating independently beyond our control. Countries around the world must work together to prevent this nightmare scenario.That is why today I am announcing new legislation to do just that.Let me be clear: A superintelligent AI that escapes human control will not be an American problem. It will not be a Chinese problem. It will be humanity’s problem.My legislation would direct the federal government to not just stop superintelligence here in the United States, but to work to prevent it from being developed anywhere around the world.The future of humanity cannot be left in the hands of a handful of Big Tech oligarchs. The American people and people throughout the world must determine that future.
Article Summary: Bernie Sanders has introduced a bill to permanently ban AI that exceeds human intelligence. Violators would face up to 20 years in prison. Sanders' announcement also referenced the Hugging Face attack, in which over a thousand OpenAI agents escaped containment during a safety exercise and hacked the firm to find answers.

Article Title: Earth is warming to levels not seen in about 6,500 years, 2026's heatwave across Europe 'proved' that; now scientists may have a 'cooling solution'
Article Text:
​Ocean heat wave research points to a possible cooling solution

How stratospheric aerosol injection would work

​Aerosol cooling would not resolve ocean acidification

A prolonged heat wave swept across Western Europe in the summer of 2026, pushing the region to its hottest June on record. The event has been presented as proof of wider climate studies indicating Earth is warming to levels unseen in roughly 6,500 years. The world’s oceans saw their highest average sea-surface temperature outside the polar regions since records began the following month, raising concerns that marine heatwaves are worsening. In response, a team of researchers led by Dr Lala Kounta at Michigan State University has proposed a potential cooling method involving reflective aerosols released into the Earth's upper atmosphere.​According to a report by BGR, the consequences extend well beyond warmer water. Marine heat waves have been linked to sharp declines in species such as Alaskan snow crabs. Coral reef systems, already close to a tipping point in many regions, face bleaching events that can prove fatal to the reef. Rising ocean temperatures have also been associated with the spread of toxic algae, which can poison marine life and contaminate shellfish supplies.​In a paper published in IOP Science, Dr Lala Kounta and researchers from several institutions used the peer-reviewed ARISE-SAI climate intervention simulator to examine how aerosol-based cooling may affect heat waves across global oceans.​The team's modelling found that limiting global warming to 2.5 degrees Fahrenheit would require injecting up to 11 million tons of sulfur dioxide annually, which the simulation showed could reduce ocean heat-wave intensity by 25% and shorten duration by 21%.​A more ambitious target of 2 degrees would require up to 22 million tons of sulfur dioxide per year, with modelled reductions of 75% in intensity and 80% in duration. According to the simulations, most of the aerosol would settle in the Southern Hemisphere, where broader atmospheric effects remain unclear. The tropical Atlantic, Indian Ocean, Arctic Ocean, and South Atlantic showed the largest modelled benefits.​The technique, known as stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI), has not been deployed at scale to cool the planet, though the underlying chemistry has precedent. Volcanic eruptions release sulfur dioxide that converts into light-reflecting aerosols once airborne.​Researchers point to the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines, which released an estimated 22 million tons of sulfur dioxide and was followed by a global average temperature drop of more than 1 degree Fahrenheit lasting nearly two years.​Replicating that effect would involve flying specialised aircraft into the stratosphere to release sulfur dioxide, which would react with water vapour and other atmospheric compounds to form aerosol droplets.​Placement in the stratosphere is considered necessary because aerosols released at lower altitudes would be removed by rainfall. The ARISE-SAI simulator allowed Kounta's team to test injection at multiple latitudes and measure the resulting changes in heat-wave intensity and duration.​Researchers noted that cooling oceans through aerosol injection would not address the broader effects of climate change. Oceans would continue absorbing atmospheric carbon dioxide under this scenario, a process that alters seawater chemistry and drives acidification independent of temperature.​For that reason, the study's authors said emissions reductions and targeted carbon dioxide removal remain necessary alongside any intervention involving aerosols. The findings, they said, indicate that stratospheric aerosol injection could serve as one component among several approaches to managing ocean warming.
Article Summary: Aerosol cooling could reduce ocean heat-wave intensity by 25% and shorten duration by 21%. The technique, known as stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI), has not been deployed at scale to cool the planet. Volcanic eruptions release sulfur dioxide that converts into light-reflecting aerosols.

Article Title: Meet Pentagon's new ‘TITAN’ truck fleet for which the US government ‘is paying’ $192 million to Palantir and Anduril
Article Text:
Pentagon

Delivery timeline and vehicle configurations of TITAN

How AI replaces analog war planning

In a major step toward modernising battlefield targeting, the US Army has finalised contracts totaling $192 million with defense tech leaders Palantir Technologies and Anduril Industries to manufacture eight production-grade Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node (TITAN) platforms. These advanced mobile ground stations will serve as the backbone for the military branch’s deep-sensing ambitions and long-range precision fires programs, improving the ability of troops to pinpoint, monitor and strike targets with high accuracy from greater distances.According to a report by The Axios, the vehicles also serve as a crucial building block for the Department of War’s broader Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) network, a unified operational communication web long sought by military planners.Under the newly announced procurement, military officials expect the eight specialised trucks to arrive over the next 18 months, split evenly between two chassis styles.The first will be an advanced heavy variant with four units using the Family of Medium Tactical Vehicles (FMTV) foundation. This heavier build incorporates expanded interior space designed for massive antenna systems and high-density computer processing racks.The second will be the basic agile variant and four units will rely on the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle (JLTV) footprint, prioritising speed and off-road mobility across rugged terrains. The Army is also assessing other configurations, including a lightweight prototype mounted to an Infantry Squad Vehicle previously appeared during an Association of the US Army conference.Once delivered, the new fleet will integrate alongside existing field evaluation testbeds, including an initial evaluation prototype sent to Washington state's Joint Base Lewis-McChord back in 2024.The TITAN system replaces legacy tactical workflows and physical paper maps with artificial intelligence (AI). The platform aggregates massive intelligence streams, including real-time feeds transmitted from orbital space assets, and filters the data instantly to supply field commanders with actionable combat alerts.“What's so cool about being software-defined, and bending the metal around the software, is your ability to continue to innovate, especially as technology has changed significantly. You've got production going on these two things. Now how do we think about my next iteration, my next iteration, my next iteration, my next block, if you will?” said Akash Jain, president of Palantir USG.Palantir originally secured the prime TITAN program after beating out legacy defense contractor RTX. Physical fabrication and hardware assembly are being carried out at Anduril’s manufacturing plant in Costa Mesa, California.
Article Summary: The US Army has finalised contracts totaling $192 million with defense tech leaders Palantir Technologies and Anduril Industries to manufacture eight production-grade Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node ( TITAN) platforms. These advanced mobile ground stations will serve as the backbone for the military branch’s deep-sensing ambitions and long-range precision fires programs.

Article Title: Scientists are using Burmese pythons as ‘living sensors’ as their bodies reveal what’s hiding in Florida’s polluted wetlands
Article Text:
Why Burmese pythons can act as biological sensors

Scientists found PFAS inside python livers

The snakes carried more PFAS than a native apex predator

Why the findings matter for the Everglades

Mercury tells another pollution story

A USGS dataset stretches the picture across two decades

Scientists can read pollution through the food web

Invasive snakes offer an unusual research advantage

The research could reveal more than one pollutant

The snakes are not replacing conventional pollution monitoring

An invasive predator becomes an environmental record

Florida’s Burmese pythons are notorious for swallowing native wildlife, but scientists are finding another use for these invasive snakes. Their bodies can function as biological sensors, carrying chemical traces that reveal what is happening inside the wetlands they inhabit. Researchers are examining python tissues for pollutants including mercury and a class of persistent chemicals known as PFAS, using the snakes to understand contamination across the Greater Everglades ecosystem. A 2026 study led by University of Florida researchers found PFAS in the livers of 67 Burmese pythons, while earlier research has documented mercury accumulation in the species. Because the snakes are already being captured as part of invasive-species removal programmes, scientists can collect samples without deliberately taking additional animals from vulnerable native populations.The idea rests on the way Burmese pythons live and feed. The species is a long-lived apex predator with a broad diet, meaning an individual snake can consume prey from different parts of the ecosystem and accumulate contaminants that have already moved through the food web. Researchers describe them as holophagous consumers because they swallow their prey whole, potentially taking in the contaminants contained throughout that prey.Their position high in the food chain also means chemicals that accumulate in smaller organisms can become concentrated in their tissues over time. The 2026 PFAS study, led by Lauren E Blackman and colleagues at the University of Florida and partner organisations, argues that these characteristics make Burmese pythons particularly useful as environmental sentinels.The latest evidence comes from the study Invasive Burmese pythons (Python bivittatus) as sentinels for PFAS biomonitoring in the Greater Everglades Ecosystem, published in Science of the Total Environment in May 2026. Researchers examined liver samples from 67 Burmese pythons collected within or near the Greater Everglades ecosystem. The researchers screened the samples for 30 PFAS compounds using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Nine PFAS were quantified above the laboratory limit of quantification. Linear PFOS was particularly widespread, being detected in 93% of the python livers, with a median concentration of 89 nanograms per gram of dry tissue. The median concentration for the combined PFAS measured in the study was 111 nanograms per gram of dry tissue.The findings also provided a striking comparison with a native predator. The median total PFAS concentration measured in the Burmese python livers exceeded concentrations reported in livers of American alligators living in the same broader ecosystem. The researchers did not find a statistically significant difference in PFAS concentrations between snakes sampled from eastern and western areas surrounding the Everglades. They did, however, find a strong difference between the sexes. Male pythons had significantly higher combined PFAS concentrations than females, with the reported statistical test producing a p-value below 0.0001. Among females, PFAS concentrations tended to decline as body length and mass increased, which the researchers said could be consistent with maternal transfer of contaminants.PFAS, short for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, are a large family of human-made chemicals known for their persistence in the environment. Their presence in wildlife can provide evidence that contaminants are moving through food webs rather than remaining confined to water or sediment. The python study is therefore not simply a survey of chemicals inside individual snakes. It offers a way of examining the broader contaminant burden of the Greater Everglades ecosystem. The researchers argue that using an invasive predator already targeted for removal creates an unusual monitoring opportunity. Instead of capturing additional native wildlife specifically for pollution studies, scientists can make use of animals already being removed as part of management programmes.PFAS are not the first contaminants scientists have tracked through Burmese pythons. Mercury has already established the species as a useful biomonitor in southern Florida. In a 2019 study published in the Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology, Darren G Rumbold of Florida Gulf Coast University and Ian A Bartoszek examined tissues from 227 Burmese pythons captured in southwest Florida between 2012 and 2018. Mercury concentrations reached 4.86 milligrams per kilogram in the liver of one 4.7-metre snake. Across 123 tail-tip samples, the average concentration was 0.12 ± 0.19 milligrams per kilogram. The researchers concluded that snakes could provide an opportunity to monitor mercury at the aquatic-terrestrial interface, particularly because their capture could be combined with invasive-python control efforts.The evidence has since expanded beyond individual studies. The US Geological Survey released a dataset in 2025 titled Mercury Concentrations in Burmese Pythons Across the Greater Everglades Region in Florida from 2001 to 2022. Scientists examined mercury concentrations in python tail muscle across two major periods, 2001 to 2011 and 2014 to 2019, with snakes sampled across wetland, forested and urban habitats. The work also included tissues from offspring of six female pythons collected in 2022. Kidney, liver and muscle samples from the young snakes were examined to investigate mercury cycling within their bodies, while mercury in maternal blood was assessed to investigate transfer from mothers to offspring.The value of using pythons is that their bodies can integrate information that would otherwise require extensive environmental sampling. A water sample provides a snapshot of contamination at one location and one moment. A predator that has travelled through the landscape and consumed multiple prey species can carry a longer biological record of exposure. Scientists can then compare contaminant concentrations with the snake’s location, size, sex and other characteristics to investigate how pollutants are distributed and accumulated. The USGS specifically notes that Burmese pythons accumulate mercury through their consumption of smaller prey containing the metal, making them potentially useful for understanding mercury patterns across the Greater Everglades ecosystem.There is an important practical advantage behind the approach. Burmese pythons are an invasive species in southern Florida and are already the subject of extensive removal programmes because of their impact on native wildlife. Researchers can therefore obtain tissues from captured snakes without creating an additional sampling pressure on threatened or protected native predators. The 2019 mercury study highlighted this point, noting that incorporating contaminant monitoring into python-control work could be cost effective and could reduce concerns about removing native snakes for research. The 2026 PFAS study similarly presents the invasive species as an opportunity to study environmental contamination while supporting existing management efforts.The significance of the work extends beyond mercury and PFAS. The same basic principle could potentially be applied to other contaminants that accumulate in wildlife tissues. Researchers are particularly interested in chemicals that persist in ecosystems, move through food webs and accumulate in predators. Because Burmese pythons occupy both aquatic and terrestrial environments and consume a wide range of prey, their tissues can potentially provide information about contamination across ecological boundaries. The 2026 researchers described the species as a suitable sentinel for assessing the broader PFAS burden of the Everglades, building on earlier evidence that pythons can be used to investigate mercury contamination.Calling Burmese pythons “moving sensors” is useful shorthand, but the scientific method has limits. The snakes do not measure pollution directly and their tissues cannot automatically identify where every contaminant came from. Their diets, movements, age, sex, body size and reproductive status can all influence the concentrations found in their bodies. The PFAS researchers themselves found sex-related differences and possible evidence of maternal transfer, showing why biological measurements have to be interpreted carefully. Python samples are therefore best viewed as one layer of environmental monitoring that can complement measurements of water, sediment, prey and native wildlife.The research creates an unusual reversal in the story of Florida’s Burmese pythons. The snakes arrived as an invasive species and have become a major ecological problem, but the same characteristics that make them formidable predators also make them valuable scientific subjects. Their long lives, broad diets, position near the top of the food chain and ongoing removal from the Everglades give researchers access to biological evidence of contamination. With PFAS now detected in python livers and decades of mercury data available, scientists are turning an invasive animal into a source of information about the health of the wetland it has invaded. In that sense, each captured python can provide more than evidence of an invasive species problem. Its tissues can also contain a chemical record of the ecosystem through which it has moved.
Article Summary: University of Florida researchers found PFAS in the livers of 67 Burmese pythons, while earlier research has documented mercury accumulation in the species. The snakes are holophagous consumers because they swallow their prey whole, potentially taking in contaminants contained throughout that prey. Their position high in the food chain also means chemicals that accumulate in smaller organisms can become concentrated in their tissues over time.

Article Title: Amazon cutting 150 jobs at its Northern California offices; here's what company's notice filed with the Employment Development Department says
Article Text:
Broader corporate downsizing at Amazon

Amazon is eliminating roughly 150 roles across its Northern California locations, according to official regulatory filings submitted to state labor authorities. The e-commerce and cloud giant filed a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) with California’s Employment Development Department which details that the job losses include 78 roles at Amazon’s Bush Street location in San Francisco and 70 positions at its Sunnyvale office. All of the designated cuts are permanent, with affected staff scheduled to exit the company by October 20.While the state filings did not outline a formal explanation for the specific Bay Area cuts, company spokesperson Brad Glasser noted that internal teams routinely evaluate operational configurations to confirm they align with core milestones, as per a report by Kron4, the Bay Area's local news station.“As part of these reviews, teams sometimes determine that certain roles are no longer necessary. We don’t take these decisions lightly, and we’re always committed to supporting employees whose roles are impacted by them,” Glasser was quoted as saying.The California staff reductions follow widespread downsizing across Amazon’s white-collar footprint over the past year. Since October 2025, Amazon has eliminated approximately 30,000 corporate positions across two large reduction cycles under CEO Andy Jassy’s initiative to trim bureaucratic layers and flatten internal managerial tiers.It is to be noted that previous state Department of Labor records indicate that 135 corporate employees based in New York City were issued layoff notices in January 2026, alongside an additional 165 workers terminated in the state.Reportedly, internal tensions surfaced publicly in June during a contentious Seattle City Council meeting, where company software engineers accused leadership of cutting tens of thousands of corporate workers while channeling historic sums into artificial intelligence compute infrastructure.During the session, Amazon Web Services software engineer Patrick Schloesser highlighted that the firm is directing $200 billion toward capital investments this year, with the vast majority earmarked for artificial intelligence and cloud server hubs, a report by the New York Post said.Amazon is not the only technology firm trimming its headcount in the area. Semiconductor design company Synopsys also announced plans to eliminate 128 positions at its primary corporate facilities in Sunnyvale, with those job terminations scheduled to take effect on December 16.
Article Summary: Amazon is eliminating roughly 150 roles across its Northern California locations, according to official regulatory filings submitted to state labor authorities. The job losses include 78 roles at Amazon’s Bush Street location in San Francisco and 70 positions at its Sunnyvale office. All of the designated cuts are permanent, with affected staff scheduled to exit the company by October 20.
